title: Transient siRNA-mediated protein knockdown in mouse followed by liver tissue analysis
author: Wrobel, Siddiqi, et al.
materials: SuperScript III First Strand Synthesis System

In this protocol we used Invivofectamine™ 3.0 Reagent (ThermoFisher) and in vivo siRNA from Ambion. Alternatively, one could use in vivo-jetPEI® (Polyplus transfection) or AteloGene® (Bio-connect). 1.Calculating systemic amount and concentration of siRNA for a 1 mg/kg and 2 mg/kg dose.a.To dose each mouse according to its individual body weight (in mg/kg), the siRNA amount and its micromolar (μM) concentration has to be calculated.b.Before proceeding, convert the concentration of the siRNA stock to mg/mL (for example, use online calculator: https://horizondiscovery.com/en/ordering-and-calculation-tools/nmol-to-ug-calculator). In our study, we used 250 μM siRNA stock solution (Table 1).c.Weigh the mice a day prior to the experiment. This is necessary, as the Invivofectamine/siRNA complex takes 24 h to form.Note: In this protocol, we injected 200 μl per mouse. Always prepare ×1.5 volume per injection as a backup in case of any spillage.2.Preparation of Invivofectamine 3.0 - siRNA duplex complex mixture 24 h prior injectiona.To determine the siRNA concentration for each individual mouse, we made use of the information worked out in Table 1 and kept all mouse records in an MS Excel file.b.The siRNA duplex solution for injection is prepared in accordance with the ThermoFisher protocol for Invivofectamine 3.0 Reagent Complexation with slight modifications.c.Mix siRNA duplex solution (as calculated in the column 5 of Table 1) with Complexation Buffer in 1:1 ratio.d.Thaw the Invivofectamine 3.0 reagent at 20°C–25°C and add to the diluted siRNA in 1: 0.5 ratio (modified from original manufacturer protocol).e.Vortex immediately to ensure Invivofectamine 3.0 complexation.f.Incubate invivofectamine 3.0- siRNA duplex mixture at 50oC, for 30 min.g.Spin the tubes briefly to collect the sample at the bottom of the tube.h.Dilute the sample by adding PBS, pH 7.4 (DNase RNase free) to a total volume of 200 μl.i.Store the solution for 24 h at 4°C.CRITICAL: Use RNase-free tubes, RNase-free filter pipette tips and follow standard biological sterile techniques.

steps.title: Prepare mouse cohort
steps.instruction: House C57BL/6J male and female mice (7–10 weeks, ~20–30 g) 3–5 per cage on a 12 h light/dark cycle with ad lib food and water; for the main study use at least 8–10 mice of each gender per condition.

steps.title: Prepare siRNA stock solution
steps.instruction: Spin siRNA‑containing tubes, resuspend in UltraPure DNase/RNase‑free distilled water, vortex briefly, aliquot into RNase‑free tubes and store at –80 °C; use RNase‑free filter tips and sterile technique throughout.

steps.title: Prepare RIPA lysis buffer (50 mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl (150 mM final), 5 mL 10 % Triton X‑100 (1 % final), 2.5 mL 10 % sodium deoxycholate (0.5 % final, protect from light), 250 µL 20 % SDS (0.1 % final), 2.5 mL 1 M Tris pH 8.0 (50 mM final), add RNase‑free water to 38.5 mL, bring volume to 50 mL; store aliquots at –20 °C and add protease/phosphatase inhibitors fresh before use.

steps.title: Calculate siRNA dose per mouse
steps.instruction: Weigh each mouse a day before injection; for a 20 g mouse a 1 mg/kg dose requires 0.025 mg siRNA (≈0.93 µL of 250 µM stock) and a 2 mg/kg dose requires 0.041 mg (≈1.85 µL); prepare 1.5 × the 200 µL injection volume as backup.

steps.title: Form Invivofectamine‑siRNA complex
steps.instruction: Mix the calculated siRNA volume with an equal volume of Complexation Buffer (1:1); thaw Invivofectamine 3.0 at 20‑25 °C and add to the diluted siRNA at a 1:0.5 ratio; vortex immediately, incubate 30 min at 50 °C, spin briefly, then dilute with RNase‑free PBS pH 7.4 to a total of 200 µL; store the mixture 24 h at 4 °C and keep all consumables RNase‑free.

steps.title: Inject siRNA complex into mice
steps.instruction: Inject 200 µL of the prepared Invivofectamine‑siRNA solution into each mouse (intravenous or appropriate route) within 24 h of complex formation; keep the solution on ice until use.

steps.title: Harvest liver tissue for RNA
steps.instruction: On day 5 post‑injection, cut 50–100 mg of liver from the same lobe using scalpel and forceps cleaned with 70 % ethanol and RNase‑decontamination solution; place fragment into a pre‑cooled 2 mL RNase/DNase‑free tube with ceramic beads on dry ice; add 1 mL TRIzol per sample on ice, homogenize in a cold room, incubate 5 min at 20‑25 °C, centrifuge 12 000 × g for 10 min at 20 °C, transfer supernatant to RNase‑free tubes and store at –60 to –80 °C if needed.

steps.title: Purify RNA and synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Purify RNA using the PureLink RNA kit with on‑column DNase treatment according to the TRIzol protocol; store RNA at –80 °C; synthesize cDNA with the SuperScript III First‑Strand Synthesis System and store cDNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify gene expression by qPCR
steps.instruction: Set up real‑time PCR with PowerUp SYBR Green Master Mix using the cDNA; run according to the manufacturer’s instructions; calculate ΔCT (target vs. Gapdh) and ΔΔCT (treated vs. mixed control sample) to obtain fold‑change values.

steps.title: Harvest liver tissue for protein
steps.instruction: Cut ~100 mg of liver from the same lobe using scalpel and forceps cleaned with ethanol; wash fragment in 1 mL ice‑cold 1×PBS by inverting the tube; transfer fragment to a pre‑cooled 2 mL tube containing ceramic beads and 500 µL cold RIPA buffer (with freshly added protease/phosphatase inhibitors); keep tubes on ice.

steps.title: Extract protein lysate
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue, incubate the homogenate on ice 30 min, centrifuge 12 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, transfer the supernatant to fresh pre‑cooled tubes and keep on ice.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration with the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit following the manufacturer’s protocol; aliquot and store lysates at –80 °C to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Perform SDS‑PAGE and Western blot
steps.instruction: Load equal amounts of protein on SDS‑PAGE, run the gel, transfer to a membrane and probe with antibodies against Usp9x and a housekeeping protein (Tubulin or Gapdh); stain the gel with Coomassie to verify equal loading; quantify band intensities as arbitrary units normalized to the housekeeping signal.
